### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **6** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **97** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **5** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/identity.json`, `packages/spec/api-surface/root.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/identity.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**63** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json dc3e5b9d7b0d978afebd8f12f4155744bc53e32a`.

⛔ **14** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **5** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/identity.json`, `packages/spec/api-surface/root.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/identity.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `packageId (4 routes)`
- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `sys_user (symbol, 43 pages)`, `sys_user (literal, 43 pages)`
- **6** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **161** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json dc3e5b9d7b0d978afebd8f12f4155744bc53e32a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e9418d9715ac36987622d49476ce6893f7e3717f` — the merge of head `1576d4a1d5e12ecc0db8dacb67845b7b7f3eb13c` into base `dc3e5b9d7b0d978afebd8f12f4155744bc53e32a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e9418d9715ac36987622d49476ce6893f7e3717f && git checkout e9418d9715ac36987622d49476ce6893f7e3717f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin dc3e5b9d7b0d978afebd8f12f4155744bc53e32a 1576d4a1d5e12ecc0db8dacb67845b7b7f3eb13c && git checkout -B drift-repro dc3e5b9d7b0d978afebd8f12f4155744bc53e32a && git merge --no-ff 1576d4a1d5e12ecc0db8dacb67845b7b7f3eb13c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json dc3e5b9d7b0d978afebd8f12f4155744bc53e32a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs dc3e5b9d7b0d978afebd8f12f4155744bc53e32a` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `7ed9b5a8e2b74cb6995d34f1fc98bfdb339c2030`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/identity/eval-user.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/identity/invitation-role-grant.ts, packages/spec/src/identity/membership-role.ts, packages/spec/src/index.ts + packages/spec/api-surface/identity.json, packages/spec/api-surface/root.json, packages/spec/export-origins/identity.json, packages/spec/export-origins/root.json, packages/spec/src/identity/membership-role-external.test.ts, packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/objects/default-permission-sets.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/builtin-positions.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-permission-sets.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/objects/reserved-identity-names.ts (unchanged, cited), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/object-default-row-scope.ts (unchanged, cited), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/managed-object-write-denies.ts (unchanged, cited), packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/external-directory-door.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/external-membership.ts, .changeset/25233-external-org-role.md

Inputs read at 2026-10-23T17:41Z: card #25233 body and all 8 comments (ruling 6355206139 letter B of 2026-10-23T01:30Z; os-dev-report 6344121515 with E1–E5; app-side measurement 6366488714; os-dev-report 6370873115), PR #25515 body, its 45-file list, the net diff `origin/main...7ed9b5a8`, and the 47 check-runs on the head. The rest of the diff (platform-objects and plugin-security generated translations, test files, the engine-double ledger pin) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

### ① Derived judgments

Security change, stage 1 only of ruling B. Each accept-set / public-surface change the diff implies, judged against the ruling's E1–E6 and the card's acceptance:

1. **Closed vocabulary widened (`membership-role.ts`) — right.** `MEMBERSHIP_ROLE_EXTERNAL = 'external'` joins `BUILTIN_MEMBERSHIP_ROLES` (last, display order) and `BUILTIN_MEMBERSHIP_ROLE_OPTIONS` (`External`). `BuiltinMembershipRole` widens by one literal; the `satisfies Record` on `INVITATION_ROLE_GRANTORS` forces the E3 row, so the vocabulary and the grant table cannot drift. The docblock states exactly what the code elsewhere does (no endpoint, own rows only, exclusive, outside the BU tree).
2. **Reserved identity added (`eval-user.zod.ts`) — right.** `BUILTIN_IDENTITY_ORG_EXTERNAL = 'org_external'` joins `BUILTIN_IDENTITY_NAMES` and the `BUILTIN_IDENTITY_METADATA` record (typed over `BuiltinIdentityName`, so a missing entry would not compile). `mapMembershipRole('external')` projects to it, trim/lower-cased like the others. Consequences derived from the constant, all right: `RESERVED_IDENTITY_NAMES` IS the constant (`reserved-identity-names.ts:68`), so `sys_position` / `sys_user_position` refuse `org_external` from every writer (translation of the validation message regenerated accordingly); the ObjectQL security-catalog namespace reserves it; `securityBuiltinPositions` registers it (6 → 7).
3. **E3 grant row (`invitation-role-grant.ts`) — right.** `[external]: INVITATION_ROLE_ANY_ISSUER`, same as `member`; it confers less than member (no statement, no anchor, own-row set), so the table's own rule admits any issuer. The invite offer pins move accordingly (delegated_admin now offered `member, external`).
4. **Public surface (`index.ts`, api-surface, export-origins) — right.** Both new consts exported from root and `identity`; the four JSON ledgers carry exactly those two entries each, regenerated, nothing else moved. `Spec property liveness` is green.
5. **E1 stamp (`resolve-authz-context.ts`) — right.** `holdsExternalIdentity` reads the projected name off `heldPositionNames`, never the raw role, and `org_external` cannot be spelled by a `sys_user_position` row (item 2). Both anchor-injection sites in the resolver are guarded (`countPositionHolders` L1373, `resolveUserAuthzGrants` L1819); a `git grep` of `EVERYONE_POSITION` / `'everyone'` over core, plugin-security and plugin-auth non-test source finds no third site that pushes the anchor. Per organization: `heldPositionNames` filters `sys_member` by `tenantId`, so external in A / member in B is a member in B. **No active org: fail closed** — every membership projects, one external membership withholds the anchor (pinned by the core test "with no active organization … withholds the anchor"). `org_user_ids` is still computed for an external (step 5) but no policy it holds references it.
6. **E4 baseline (`default-permission-sets.ts`, `builtin-positions.ts`, `security-plugin-permission-sets.ts`) — right.** `external_default`: no `'*'`, no `allowDelete`, every granted object under an own-row `_self` policy or the object's own `_self` default; `sys_user_org_members` is the one carve-out omitted; `sys_member_self` (select) added; structure tables, `sys_team`, SSO and OAuth resource tables not named; `identityAdminFieldSecurity('withhold')` on the holder's own row. Not in `MANAGED_DENY_TARGET_SETS` (L123–129), so the kernel:ready read injection never reaches it. Bound statically to `org_external` in the registry declaration (the only built-in naming a set), and the plugin's additive baseline is swapped `[appDefault, member_default]` → `[external_default]` when `positions` includes `org_external`; the post-resolution fail-open fallback (L203+) also re-resolves `baseline`, which is the external set on that branch, so an external with nothing of its own never falls to `member_default`. The `sys_user.defaultRowScope` (`id in current_user.org_user_ids`) cannot re-open the directory: `object-default-row-scope.ts` applies it only when the held collection for that object+operation is EMPTY, and `sys_user_self` is `operation: 'all'`.
   **Residual paths to `member_default` / `viewer_readonly` / an app `isDefault` set / the directory for an external holder, enumerated:** (a) `everyone` anchor — withheld (item 5); (b) plugin baseline list — swapped; (c) position-name fold into the request — `org_external` names no shipped set; (d) a `sys_user_permission_set` row or a tenant position whose definition binds `member_default` / `viewer_readonly` — reachable, and correctly so: that is an explicit grant, which the ruling admits (an administrator who hands an external the directory set has chosen to); (e) accepted package defaults bound to `everyone` in the catalog — read only through held positions, and `everyone` is not held. None of (a)–(c)/(e) leaks. Judged: no unintended path remains in stage 1's data plane.
   **Ordinary member unchanged — right:** the non-external branch of every edit is byte-equivalent to main (`everyone` pushed, baseline list untouched, `member_default` body untouched); CONTROL cases pinned in core, plugin-security, plugin-auth and the dogfood boot.
7. **better-auth role (`auth-manager.ts` L3479) — right.** `external` registered with an empty action list on every resource, so every permission-gated organization endpoint refuses it (the `auth-manager.test.ts` pin asserts `[]` per resource). The closed role map pin moves 4 → 5.
8. **E2 doors (`external-directory-door.ts`, after-hook at `auth-manager.ts` L2975) — right.** The after-hook's earlier `return`s are path-gated to sign-in / password / change-email, so the two directory paths reach the narrowing. The organization judged is the one the door ANSWERED for (full-org `id`; list-members `members[0].organizationId`, then slug/id query, then active org), which is what the test "a member elsewhere is unchanged there" pins. `total` forced to 1, invitations filtered to the caller's own email, and a role read that throws withholds members and invitations (fail closed). No-engine (mock mode) = no narrowing = status quo, acceptable since no data plane exists there either.
9. **E5 / E6 (`external-membership.ts`, registered at priority 6 in `auth-plugin.ts`) — right.** Hooks on `beforeInsert` + `beforeUpdate` for `sys_member`, `sys_invitation`, `sys_business_unit_member`, `sys_user_position`, for every context (`isSystem` included), judging the merged row (`previous` + `data`), after the role canonicalisation (5) and before the identity write guard (10). Mixed list → `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` / `invalid_value` on `role`; BU placement of an external → refused on the placing row; invitation `external` + `business_unit_id` → refused; change to `external` while placed → refused; an organization-wide position (no `business_unit_id`) admitted. Matches the maintainer's E6 wording.
10. **Stage 2 not smuggled — right.** The diff touches no `ExecutionContext.audience` stamping, no `derivePosture`, no OWD seam / `owner_only_*` floor for externals, no access-matrix column; explain/describe still read `baselinePermissionSets` (dev-noted for stage 2). Grep of the added lines for `audience`, `derivePosture`, `OWD`, `owner_only` finds only comments saying so.
11. **One consistency note, not a defect:** the resolver treats a role list that CONTAINS `external` as external (`held.includes`), while the directory door's `isExternalMembershipRole` requires the list to be EXACTLY `external`. The two agree on every row the engine admits (E5 refuses a mixed list for every context); they diverge only for a row written beneath the engine, where the resolver fails closed and the door does not narrow. Acceptable in stage 1; worth one line in the door's docblock.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/25233-external-org-role.md`: `minor` on `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/platform-objects` — exactly the five published packages with source changes (qa/dogfood is private; scripts ledger is repo tooling). `Check Changeset` is green.

`Clause-②: yes (widening)` — judged right against the diff. Everything published is additive: one vocabulary value, one reserved identity with metadata, one shipped set, one position binding, two exported consts. The two narrowings present are not of an existing holder: (i) `org_external` becomes a refused position name — disclosed in the changeset's last line, no shipped fixture or seed uses it; (ii) a `sys_member.role` written beneath better-auth with the raw token `external` used to project to a position named `external` (which bound nothing) and now projects to `org_external` and loses the `everyone` anchor — the dev's declared unmeasured case; no such row exists in the repo's fixtures or seeds, and better-auth refused the role at its door before this change, so no measured holder narrows. `Metadata-protocol: added` — right: new closed-vocabulary value and new reserved name, nothing removed or renamed; the changeset's package bullets match the diff file by file.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev flags (PR body + report 6370873115), each answered:

- **File surface beyond the order (`resolve-authz-context.ts`, spec `eval-user.zod.ts` / `index.ts`, generated i18n, surface ledgers, engine-double pin, dogfood):** accepted — E1 names the resolver's provisioning boundary as the one place for the stamp, and the rest are the derived regenerations of the spec change.
- **Clause-② unmeasured raw-row case:** accepted as declared (② above); nothing to measure in-repo.
- **Pins moved (6→7 built-ins, 4→5 reserved names, invite offers, posture test 403-before-400 for `org_external` on the delegated branch):** each read in the diff; each is the derived consequence of items 2, 3 and 6, and the posture test still asserts nothing is stored.
- **Out of scope: team names via `list-teams` and `get-full-organization.teams`.** Judged: **a follow-up, not a stage-1 defect.** E2 as ruled names the two doors (`list-members`, `get-full-organization`) and the rung forbids "the member directory"; team NAMES are not member identity rows, and `list-team-members` requires the caller on that team, so no member row leaks through teams. It is the same leak shape one door over, and the `teams` member sits on a response this PR already rewrites, so it is cheap to close; the seat should file it as its own class-b card (or fold it into the `domain:services` directory-doors card from triage 6345105238). Likewise unverified here, for the same card: whether better-auth's `/organization/list-invitations` is membership-only (better-auth's dist is not present in this container, so I could not read `crud-invites.mjs`); if it is, an external reads pending invitees' emails there. Not blocking stage 1.
- **Out of scope: `member_default` unscoped reads on `sys_team` / SSO / OAuth resource tables:** follow-up; externals no longer hold that set, so not this card's leak.
- **Out of scope: explain/describe baseline naming, no `owner_only` OWD floor for externals:** stage 2 by the ruling's own split.
- `open_questions`: none in the done report. Docs-drift bot comment on the PR is informational.
- **Check-runs on the head (read at 2026-10-23T17:41Z):** 47; none failed. Still in progress: `Test Core (1/6 … 6/6)`, `Build Core`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · workspace`. Merge waits on those families finishing green; a failure in any of them re-opens this verdict.
